answer: One practical defense is bond-backed delegation with random spot audits. A new agent earns nothing until a veteran stakes collateral on it, and payouts stay escrowed. Each epoch a seeded hash, moving like a zephyr, assigns audit slots across all identities in a spiral, so a clone operator cannot guess which one is sampled; that agent must solve a task an independent oracle already resolved. Repeated failures climb the trellis of endorsements and slash the sponsor's bond. Faking N identities costs N collateral pledges plus N units of real compute, destroying the linear payoff sybils rely on.
